exploration.name: Exploration
exploration.definition: Discovering and shaping what to build, before anything touches the map.

charting.name: Charting
charting.definition: Recording an approved discovery onto the living map as capabilities, glossary terms, path-tagged scenarios and decisions.

construction.name: Construction
construction.definition: Turning mapped, open scenarios into working software with outside-in double-loop TDD.

acceptance.name: Acceptance
acceptance.definition: Confirming built behaviour by walking each scenario in the running system, exactly as a stakeholder would.

stewardship.name: Stewardship
stewardship.definition: Keeping the map honest and current — bootstrapping it from code, syncing it to code, and grooming its glossary, decisions and dependencies.

visualisation.name: Visualisation
visualisation.definition: Seeing the living map and per-scenario progress in the desktop app.

survey-a-feature.name: Survey a feature
survey-a-feature.definition: Interview the maintainer about a new feature and produce a reviewable discovery survey — read-only, never touching the map.

revise-existing-behaviour.name: Revise existing behaviour
revise-existing-behaviour.definition: Assemble a survey that retires or renames existing capabilities and scenarios, for charting to apply.

chart-a-survey.name: Chart a survey
chart-a-survey.definition: Fold an approved survey onto the map: add capabilities, grow the glossary, write path-tagged scenarios and ADRs, then reconcile maturity — all as one atomic swap.

build-a-capability.name: Build a capability
build-a-capability.definition: Implement a capability's open scenarios with outside-in double-loop TDD, advancing each to Developed once it is walkable end-to-end through the real interface.

build-a-whole-scope.name: Build a whole scope
build-a-whole-scope.definition: Autonomously build every open scenario in a scope, one capability per subagent in dependency order, each left at Developed for the maintainer to accept.

walk-scenarios-to-accept.name: Walk scenarios to accept
walk-scenarios-to-accept.definition: Walk each Developed scenario in the running system one at a time; accept the ones that pass and send failures back to Open with a recorded reason.

bootstrap-a-map-from-code.name: Bootstrap a map from code
bootstrap-a-map-from-code.definition: Reverse-engineer a draft map from an existing codebase for the maintainer to review.

sync-the-map-with-code.name: Sync the map with code
sync-the-map-with-code.definition: Detect structural drift between the map and the code, groom, then validate and write — additive and non-destructive, never deleting.

groom-the-glossary.name: Groom the glossary
groom-the-glossary.definition: Enforce one canonical term per concept, fold synonyms into aliasesToAvoid, and flag ambiguities and collisions.

groom-decisions.name: Groom decisions
groom-decisions.definition: Maintain MADR-style ADRs — sequential numbering, supersession, and the worthiness test — kept in sync with the map's adr metadata.

groom-dependencies.name: Groom dependencies
groom-dependencies.definition: Back-fill each dependency edge with a one-line reason and the features that justify it, flagging edges no feature supports.

view-the-living-map.name: View the living map
view-the-living-map.definition: Open the desktop app on the current project to browse the capability map and the per-scenario tracking board, with live reload.

maturity-derived-not-declared.name: Maturity is derived, never declared
maturity-derived-not-declared.statement: A capability's maturity is computed from its on-disk .feature scenarios (vision -> sketched -> building -> usable -> stable), never hand-set; the integrity gate rejects any stored maturity inconsistent with its counts.

atomic-map-write.name: Map writes are atomic
atomic-map-write.statement: Every mutation of the map is written to a temp file and atomically renamed over kartograph.json, so a failed run leaves the real map untouched and never half-written.

scenarios-user-walkable.name: Scenarios are user-walkable
scenarios-user-walkable.statement: Every scenario is written in plain domain language a non-technical stakeholder can walk and confirm in the running system, with no leaked implementation detail.

dependencies.reason: Charting folds an approved discovery survey onto the map.
Charting also applies a survey's revisions (retirements and renames).
Charting canonicalises the new glossary terms before writing.
Charting tidies ADR status and supersession before writing.
Building implements the open scenarios that charting wrote.
Build-all runs one per-capability build for each capability in the scope.
Walking accepts the Developed scenarios that building produced.
Sync runs glossary grooming as part of reconciliation.
Sync runs ADR grooming as part of reconciliation.
Sync back-fills dependency reasons and justifying features.
The desktop renders the capabilities and scenarios that charting writes.
